ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic colon cancer to the liver
Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus

candidates.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma with portal vein tumor thrombus
support_spans: CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
contradict_spans: Tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were all within normal limits
candidates.why: The presence of a liver tumor with a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, along with a portal vein tumor thrombus, is suggestive of hepatocellular carcinoma.

candidates.name: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis
support_spans: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
candidates.why: The patient has a history of colorectal cancer and the appearance of a new liver lesion is consistent with metastasis.

candidates.name: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
support_spans: CTA demonstrated a liver tumor with two components: a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, and a cystic component
contradict_spans: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography showed no communication with the biliary tree, and bile cytology was negative for malignancy
candidates.why: The presence of a liver tumor with a cystic component and the absence of communication with the biliary tree could be suggestive of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
